title: Hairpin lace headband
excerpt: A stretchy loopy headband in DK yarn worked on a hairpin lace frame. A single strip is seamed at the ends to form a comfortable band with open loop sides.
sourceNotes: One hairpin lace strip seamed end to end to form a headband loop. The open side loops give a light, springy texture that stretches to fit most heads.

glossaryTerms.definition: The two outer edges of a hairpin lace strip, each holding the half-loops formed by rotating the frame. Leaving them open gives the headband its loopy texture.
Joining the two short ends of a hairpin strip with a slip stitch or whip stitch to form a continuous loop.

crochet.gaugeText: Each strip = 6 cm wide with prongs set 6 cm apart.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 54 cm circumference x 6 cm wide.

Set the frame to 6 cm. Slip starting loop onto left prong, chain 1, work 1 dc in the centre. Rotate and repeat. Continue until the strip measures 54 cm (about 45 loops each side). Remove from the frame and secure the live loops.
Use the tapestry needle to sew the cast-on end to the final row with a whip stitch through the matching loops. Weave in the ends.
